Depression

Understanding Depression

Depression can affect mood, energy, sleep, concentration, motivation, appetite, relationships, and the ability to enjoy things that normally matter.

Last updated September 19, 2026 · Editorial policy

Depression can look different from person to person

Some people feel persistently sad, while others mainly notice numbness, irritability, exhaustion, withdrawal, hopelessness, or difficulty functioning. Physical health conditions, medications, grief, trauma, and substance use can also affect mood, which is one reason a thoughtful evaluation matters.

Treatment options

Psychotherapy, lifestyle changes, social support, and medication are among the options that may be considered. Common therapy approaches include cognitive behavioral therapy, behavioral activation, interpersonal therapy, and other evidence-based methods.

Safety matters

If depression includes thoughts of suicide, self-harm, or an inability to stay safe, use urgent crisis support rather than waiting for a routine appointment.
